selectionNote: Curated, nonrepresentative research snapshot; not a success-rate sample.

cases.title: 70 years of engineering drawings, searchable in minutes
cases.summary: Engineers search decades of historical drawings for replacement parts. The company reports that searches fell from almost an hour to 4.5 minutes.
cases.evidence: A projected 90% annual reduction in drawing-search hours is a forecast, not a measured annual result.
cases.risk: Wrong drawings or model mismatches could create equipment and safety risks. Engineering verification is necessary.
cases.apply: Test retrieval accuracy on 30 known drawing-lookup questions before estimating savings.
cases.question: What should engineers verify before acting on an AI-retrieved drawing?

cases.title: Agentic software development and AI code review
cases.summary: The company reports shipping roughly 20 times more software with the same engineering team using coding agents and AI-assisted review.
cases.evidence: Self-reported output does not independently prove 20 times the delivered value or quality.
cases.risk: More code can increase security defects, testing bottlenecks and maintenance.
cases.apply: Measure completed tested changes and defect rates, not AI-generated lines of code.
cases.question: Does producing 20 times more code mean producing 20 times more value?

cases.title: Employee AI pilot with claimed strong ROI
cases.summary: A 315-person enterprise AI pilot reported approximately 14 hours saved per participant monthly; broader rollout followed.
cases.evidence: ROI and savings are pilot estimates in a vendor case study, not independently audited enterprise-wide results.
cases.risk: Self-reported time savings may not translate into actual cash savings. Confidentiality and employee data require controls.
cases.apply: Compare a narrow repetitive workflow before and after AI with quality and time measures.
cases.question: What evidence would you require before accepting a 954% ROI claim?

cases.title: AI-powered service assistants and faster resolutions
cases.summary: Google Cloud reports that Best Buy increased call containment by more than 50%, with fewer transfers between service agents.
cases.evidence: Figures are supplier-reported and do not independently establish causal impact or customer satisfaction.
cases.risk: Containment can rise without problems getting resolved; satisfaction and escalation matter.
cases.apply: Test a narrow FAQ workflow with resolution, transfer, and satisfaction measures.
cases.question: If fewer calls reach people, how do we know customers are better served?

cases.title: Advisor knowledge assistant and meeting summaries
cases.summary: Advisors use internal AI tools for retrieving firm information and preparing meeting notes and follow-up drafts.
cases.evidence: Adoption is reported by the company and vendor; it does not itself establish ROI.
cases.risk: Confidentiality, inaccuracies and meeting consent require strict controls and human review.
cases.apply: Evaluate citation accuracy against an approved knowledge base before increasing use.
cases.question: Why might retrieval evaluations matter more than a model name?

cases.title: Customer service automation with human support retained
cases.summary: Klarna says its AI assistant handled 80% of customer-service chats in 2025 while human support remained available.
cases.evidence: The figure appears in an SEC filing; it is not a customer satisfaction metric or a count of jobs eliminated.
cases.risk: Sensitive financial questions may require accessible human escalation and repeat-contact monitoring.
cases.apply: Measure complaints, repeat contacts, transfers, quality and full service cost alongside automation rate.
cases.question: Why is AI chat share not itself a success rate?

cases.title: Public-service chatbot accuracy problems and discontinuation
cases.summary: An NYC audit identified inaccurate and inconsistent chatbot guidance and oversight problems; an official report records decommissioning in February 2026.
cases.evidence: Independent government audit plus separate official disclosure document establish the reported findings and shutdown.
cases.risk: Inaccurate guidance about legal or regulatory requirements can result in consequential harm.
cases.apply: Constrain high-stakes responses to verified sources, test consistency and ensure escalation.
cases.question: Should public-service bots be launched before independent accuracy testing?

cases.title: Incorrect chatbot refund advice led to liability
cases.summary: A customer relied on inaccurate automated bereavement-fare advice. A British Columbia tribunal found Air Canada responsible.
cases.evidence: The tribunal confirmed the award but did not establish the chatbot's model or whether it used generative AI.
cases.risk: Automated policy responses can mislead customers and organizations remain accountable.
cases.apply: Audit automated guidance against official policy and provide escalation and corrections.
cases.question: Who bears responsibility when a business chatbot gives wrong information?
